note: Recast from Rocha & Cancello (2009), original in English; no measurement data. The original also notes that the “small soldiers” of the original description were in fact individuals parasitised by an acanthocephalan and that the soldier is monomorphic, a point not treated here as a character.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is distinguished from the other species of the genus by the combination of small ocelli and compound eyes and a large fontanelle; it differs from O. insignis in the scattered labral setae and the oval ocelli set far from the compound eyes, and from O. longilamina in the less prominent ocelli. The soldier is larger than O. brevipilosus, O. longilamina, O. macrocephalus and O. okeyma, with parallel sides of the head in dorsal view, whereas the sides are slightly convergent anteriorly in O. insignis and O. uncimandibularis.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes small, separated from the lower margin of the head by less than the greatest diameter of an ocellus. Ocelli kidney-shaped in dorsal view; oval in lateral view, separated from the compound eye by its least diameter. Fontanelle wide, of medium size. Head capsule with a few short hairs and setae. Labral setae not arranged in rows. Pronotum densely setose; mesonotum and metanotum with few setae, concentrated on the centre and the posterior margin. Head dark brown to pale brown, pronotum and tergites pale brown, sternites yellow, legs and wing scales pale brown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head parallel in dorsal view. Dorsal tubercle slightly prominent in lateral view, situated behind the lateral projection. Mandibles type 2, with a tooth-like process on the proximal half. Head capsule sparsely setose, short hairs denser ventrally, minute hairs scattered over the surface and denser on the posterior margin. Postmentum with setae. Surface of the pronotum with short hairs and the margins with setae; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum with setae and short hairs; abdominal tergites with short hairs and setae, the setae of the sternites longer on the posterior margin.
